title: (Re)Discover KTEQ
body:
After 55 years of broadcasting from the the campus of South Dakota Mines, KTEQ-FM is getting a little much-needed TLC.

## What's Happening

We're in the middle of a top-to-bottom refresh: new studio equipment, new programming tools, a new website (you're looking at it), and a renewed commitment to the independent radio philosophy that's defined this station since 1971, but with a greater emphasis on listener experience, student development, and sustainability. 

## Why Now

KTEQ has always been what you might generously call "scrappy." The station has gone silent and come back more than once. We've moved frequencies, rebuilt studios, and weathered every financial and logistical challenge a typical student-run station can face. 

In October 2025, during our most recent FM silence (our transmitter had to be refurbished)  we were inducted into the South Dakota Rock & Rollers Hall of Fame - a timely reminder that this little station has been a vital cultural touchstone for Rapid City for two generations now.  

Now it's time to build something that will last for the next 55 years.

## What's Coming

- **Studio renovation** through summer 2026
- **New 24/7 programming** with new specialty music blocks being added all summer. 
- **55th Anniversary** digital yearbook with year-by-year music recaps, and more! 
- **Studio grand reopening** and a return to live broadcasts during M-Week 2026
- **New fundraising opportunities** to support studio equipment upgrades and maintenance, future broadcast upgrades, and paid student positions 

Stay tuned. We're just getting started.
excerpt: 55 years in, KTEQ is launching a top-to-bottom refresh: new paint, new carpet, new equipment, but also maybe something more substantial?
author: KTEQ Staff
